// THE EXCEPTION SHAPE R4 RESERVED, RECORDED HERE AS *FLAGGED* RATHER THAN SANCTIONED.
//
// R4 allowed exactly one exception: a pre-change arm behind a workflow.GetVersion
// fence, kept so a recorded history replays. The plan's third RED instance WAS that
// shape, at pumpPausedAtRunStart. Stage 4b3 Task 3 discharged all five pump fences
// under the founder's no-production-users ruling, so the shape has ZERO production
// instances, and shipping an exception mechanism with no instance would have meant
// shipping an untested escape hatch in a gate whose whole failure mode is silence:
// any struct receive could be quieted by wrapping it in a GetVersion that always
// takes the new arm.
//
// So the shipped rule has NO exception, and this fixture is how that decision is
// held: the pre-change arm below IS a finding. If a future wave genuinely needs a
// fenced pre-change receive, the way back is to add the exception here, with this
// fixture flipped to `good_`, in the same commit as the fence — deliberately, in the
// open, and never by an allowlist of names.
package badfenced

const signalOperatorPauseRequested = "operatorPauseRequested"

type operatorPauseSignal struct{ Reason string }

func FencedEntry(ctx workflow.Context) (string, bool) {
	ch := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	return fencedPreChangeArm(ctx, ch)
}

func fencedPreChangeArm(ctx workflow.Context, ch workflow.ReceiveChannel) (string, bool) {
	if workflow.GetVersion(ctx, "some-pre-change-fence", workflow.DefaultVersion, 1) >= 1 {
		var raw any
		ch.Receive(ctx, &raw)
		return normaliseFenced(raw)
	}
	// The PRE-CHANGE body: a concrete struct on purpose, kept only so a recorded
	// history replays.
	var sig operatorPauseSignal
	if ch.ReceiveAsync(&sig) { // WANT: flagged — the exception SHAPE is NOT shipped
		return sig.Reason, true
	}
	return "", false
}

func normaliseFenced(raw any) (string, bool) {
	s, ok := raw.(string)
	return s, ok
}
